reasons.action: The brief's intent states a performed behavior — the car pulls forward — so the visual action is established by the request itself; the sole supplied reference is an audio beat reference, which cannot govern action.
reasons.medium: The medium owner is pinned by the accepted medium decision: no reference exists, so the rendering medium is request-governed.
reasons.wardrobe: No visual reference supplies observed clothing or accessory appearance, and no subject plate exists, so wardrobe ownership falls to the request with nothing to retain.
reasons.lighting: With no visual reference there is no observed lighting to preserve; the request's dark environment is the only authority over the light, so lighting is request-governed.
reasons.framing: No visual reference contains an observed camera composition, and the supplied audio beat reference and the 16:9 canvas ratio are not framing instructions; framing therefore belongs to the request.
reasons.palette: No visual reference carries observed color or tonal grading, so palette is request-governed; the request's darkness is the only tonal authority available.
